content.comment_body: Hello, I'm attempting to run [product_name] [version_no] on my computer, which uses Debian stable (buster). The installed Java version no longer supports the -Xincgc option since it's deprecated. $ java -version openjdk version "11.0.4" 2019-07-16 OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 11.0.4+11-post-Debian-1deb10u1) OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (build 11.0.4+11-post-Debian-1deb10u1, mixed mode, sharing) $ sh /opt/[product_name]/Application_64/[product_name] Unrecognized option: -Xincgc Error: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine. Error: A fatal exception has occurred. Program will exit. Which file or configuration line should I modify to disable the -Xincgc option?

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Please note that your operating system version is not officially tested by [company_name], so official support isn't available for this configuration. As a result, [product_name] may not function correctly on this OS.

analysis.insight_summary: The user has encountered a compatibility problem when launching [product_name] [version_no] on Debian Buster, specifically due to the use of the deprecated -Xincgc option in the Java Virtual Machine startup, which OpenJDK 11 no longer supports. There is also no formal guidance from [company_name] for this operating system setup.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] [version_no] to run without issues on a current Linux version (Debian Buster) and hopes configuration problems like unsupported JVM options can be addressed easily.
